“**No transaction fees**” usually means the platform doesn’t take an additional percentage of each sale. You’ll still generally pay **payment-processing fees**—for example, credit-card fees from Stripe, PayPal, Wix Payments, Square, or another processor.

### Platforms with no added platform transaction fee

| Platform | Important conditions |
|---|---|
| **WooCommerce** | No platform fee or revenue share. You pay your hosting, extensions, and payment processor’s fees. ([woocommerce.com](https://woocommerce.com/pricing/?trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block&utm_source=openai)) |
| **Ecwid** | Advertises no setup or transaction fees on its plans; payment-provider processing fees still apply. ([ecwid.com](https://www.ecwid.com/pricing?utm_source=openai)) |
| **BigCommerce** | No added fee when using an **Embedded Payment Provider**. BigCommerce now charges **0.6%–2%** on eligible orders processed through “Open Payment Providers,” depending on plan. ([bigcommerce.com](https://www.bigcommerce.com/pricing/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Wix** | Generally no separate Wix platform transaction fee for standard product sales, but Wix Payments or another processor charges processing fees. U.S. Wix Payments card processing is listed at **2.9% + $0.30**. ([support.wix.com](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-payments-administrasjonsgebyr?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Square Online** | No monthly software fee on the Square Free plan; Square charges online payment-processing fees instead—currently listed as **3.3% + $0.30** for online payments on Square Free in the U.S. ([squareup.com](https://squareup.com/us/en/pricing?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Squarespace** | Commerce Basic/Advanced—or the newer plans being rolled out as Core, Plus, and Advanced—have no commerce transaction fee. Payment processing still applies; digital products and automated tax services can have separate fees. ([support.squarespace.com](https://support.squarespace.com/hc/en-us/articles/27853679334157-Transaction-fees-and-payment-processing-rates?utm_source=openai)) |

### Conditional option

- **Shopify:** No additional Shopify transaction fee when the order is processed through Shopify Payments, Shop Pay, or certain manual payment methods. If you use an external payment provider, Shopify’s third-party transaction fee applies—currently shown as starting at **2%** on the basic tier. Payment processing fees still apply either way. ([help.shopify.com](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/your-account/manage-billing/billing-charges/types-of-charges/third-party-charges/third-party-transaction-fees?utm_source=openai))

### Best short list

- **Lowest platform fees and maximum control:** WooCommerce  
- **Easy hosted store with no platform sales cut:** Ecwid or Wix  
- **More built-in features and scalability:** BigCommerce, using an embedded processor  
- **Simple website plus store:** Squarespace Commerce  
- **Retail/POS-focused business:** Square Online  
- **Best-known all-in-one platform, if using its payment system:** Shopify  

So, if by “no transaction fees” you mean **zero fees of any kind per sale**, essentially none of these qualify for ordinary credit-card payments. If you mean **no extra fee charged by the ecommerce platform**, WooCommerce, Ecwid, Wix, Square Online, and qualifying BigCommerce/Squarespace plans are the main choices.

For most people, these are the easiest e-commerce platforms to set up without a developer:

| Platform | Best for | Ease of setup | Main trade-off |
|---|---|---:|---|
| **Shopify** | A serious store you expect to grow | **Very easy** | More commerce-focused than design-focused; costs can increase with apps |
| **Wix** | Beginners who want maximum design control | **Very easy** | Its extensive customization can become overwhelming |
| **Squarespace** | Small catalogs and visually polished brands | **Very easy** | Less robust for complex inventory and advanced selling |
| **Square Online** | Local retailers, restaurants, and sellers already using Square POS | **Extremely easy** | Less flexible for sophisticated e-commerce operations |
| **Ecwid** | Adding a store to an existing website | **Extremely easy** | Storefront customization is more limited than Shopify or Wix |
| **Big Cartel** | Artists, makers, and small product catalogs | **Extremely easy** | Not intended for large or complex stores |

### My recommendations

**Best overall: Shopify.**  
It provides templates, a drag-and-drop editor, guided setup, built-in commerce tools, and a large app ecosystem. It is the strongest choice if you want a straightforward launch but may eventually need inventory, marketing, multichannel selling, or international capabilities. ([shopify.com](https://www.shopify.com/online?utm_source=openai))

**Easiest for a beginner who cares about design: Wix.**  
Wix offers prebuilt store templates, visual editing, product galleries, inventory and order management, payments, and no-code customization. Choose it if your website content and branding matter as much as the store itself. ([wix.com](https://www.wix.com/ecommerce/seperated-header?utm_source=openai))

**Best for a beautiful, relatively simple store: Squarespace.**  
It is especially suitable for portfolios, creative businesses, services, memberships, and stores with a modest number of products. Its templates and commerce tools are designed to be customized without coding. ([support.squarespace.com](https://support.squarespace.com/hc/en-us/articles/206779077-Sell-on-Squarespace?utm_source=openai))

**Best if you sell in person too: Square Online.**  
Square lets you create an online store without coding and connect it to Square’s point-of-sale, inventory, customer, and payment systems. This makes it particularly convenient for shops, pop-ups, restaurants, and service businesses already using Square. ([squareup.com](https://squareup.com/us/en/online-store?msockid=1bc36084ea7b6f62259276d6eb156e3d&utm_source=openai))

**Best for adding commerce to an existing website: Ecwid.**  
Ecwid can create a standalone store or embed commerce into an existing site, with no coding or software installation required. ([ecwid.com](https://www.ecwid.com/online-store?utm_source=openai))

**Best for artists and makers: Big Cartel.**  
Big Cartel is deliberately streamlined for independent creators and small catalogs, with no-code store setup and simple product and order management. ([bigcartel.com](https://www.bigcartel.com/?r=ecm-bcep&utm_source=openai))

### Platforms I would not choose for maximum simplicity

**WooCommerce** can be powerful, but it runs through WordPress and generally involves hosting, plugin installation, updates, and compatibility management. It is better when you want control and already know WordPress—not when your priority is the easiest launch. ([woocommerce.com](https://woocommerce.com/document/installing-uninstalling-woocommerce/?utm_source=openai))

**Quick rule of thumb:**

- **Want the safest all-purpose choice?** Shopify  
- **Want the easiest visual website builder?** Wix  
- **Want the nicest-looking small store?** Squarespace  
- **Already use Square in person?** Square Online  
- **Already have a website?** Ecwid  
- **Selling handmade or creative work?** Big Cartel
